_contract: Shared cross-language fixture for pattern-template variable substitution. Both wasm-core/src/pattern_processor/matcher.rs's build_result() and src/utils/pattern/SemanticPatternProcessor.js's buildResult() independently substitute variable placeholders (e.g. "X", "Y") into a translated template string, and this file is the single source of truth both sides assert their real output against. Added after a production bug (2026-09-10): 赤姓老者 → template "X họ Xích" produced "Lão giả họ lão giảích" because both implementations matched the variable letter "X" anywhere it appeared in the template, including fused into the fixed word "Xích". Fixed on both sides by only substituting a variable letter that stands alone (not immediately preceded/followed by a lowercase letter) — mirrors src/utils/pattern/PatternTemplateEngine.js's isVariableChar. The Rust mirror check lives in wasm-core/src/pattern_processor/matcher.rs's mod tests::parity.

cases.name: simple_single_variable
cases.description: Baseline: one variable, standalone in the template.

cases.name: multiple_variables_each_filled_once
cases.description: Regression: a naive .replace(varName, ...) that ignores which variable a token belongs to only ever fills the first placeholder it finds literally in the template.

cases.name: repeated_variable_both_occurrences_filled
cases.description: The same variable letter appears twice as a genuine placeholder; both must be substituted.

cases.name: fused_variable_letter_suffix_not_corrupted
cases.description: Production bug case (赤姓X → "X họ Xích"): the variable letter X is immediately followed by a lowercase letter inside the fixed word "Xích" and must NOT be treated as the placeholder.

cases.name: fused_variable_letter_prefix_not_corrupted
cases.description: Mirror of the suffix case: the variable letter X is immediately preceded by a lowercase letter inside fixed text and must NOT be treated as the placeholder, even though a real standalone X elsewhere in the template must still be substituted.

cases.name: variable_at_string_end_boundary
cases.description: Standalone variable with no character after it (end of template) must still substitute correctly — exercises the next-char boundary check with no next char.

cases.name: variable_at_string_start_boundary
cases.description: Standalone variable with no character before it (start of template) must still substitute correctly — exercises the prev-char boundary check with no prev char.
